new.aliases: IAS exam; UPSC Civil Services; UPSC Prelims; IAS IPS IFS exam; CSE
new.test_date: Prelims in late May; Mains from late August
new.marking: One-third of the question's marks deducted per wrong answer; no penalty for unanswered
new.eligibility: Graduate degree from a recognised university (final-year students may apply). Age 21-32 years on 1 August of the exam year; relaxation for SC/ST, OBC, PwBD, ex-servicemen and others. General category gets 6 attempts (more for OBC/PwBD, unlimited for SC/ST within age).
new.application_fee: Rs. 100/- (no fee for women, SC/ST, PwBD); Rs. 200/- more for Mains
new.paper_pattern: Prelims: two objective papers of 200 marks each, 2 hours each, in Hindi and English. General Studies Paper-I decides who qualifies for Mains; General Studies Paper-II (CSAT) is qualifying with 33% minimum marks.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (9 written essay-type papers, 2 qualifying) → Interview/Personality Test (275 marks) → Final merit on Mains + Interview
new.remarks: Recruits for IAS, IPS, IFS and other central services. Prelims marks do not count for the final rank; vacancies change every year.

applicants.note: CSE/IFoS Prelims 2026 held 24 May 2026. PTI report quoting a UPSC statement: 8,19,732 applied; nearly 5.49 lakh (about 67%) appeared as per provisional data, so 'appeared' is rounded. All India Radio (newsonair.gov.in) also reports UPSC's figures of over 8 lakh applicants and nearly 5.49 lakh appeared. Latest official count in an Annual Report (2023-24): 10,27,514 applied and 5,96,481 appeared for CS(P) incl. IFoS(P) held in 2023-24.

vacancies.note: Approximate vacancies in Notice No. 05/2026-CSE (4 Feb 2026), including 33 for PwBD. UPSC's 18 June 2026 Prelims result press note says 1,016 vacancies were notified for CSE 2026 (revised figure); CSE 2025 had 1,087 per the same note.

new.notes: All exam details from the CSE 2026 notice (last date 24.02.2026, Prelims 24.05.2026). Mains dates from news only; given as general timing. Number of questions per Prelims paper is not stated in the notice (question papers are scanned), so marking is given as one-third of the question's marks. CSE 2026 is still running (interviews), CSE 2025 is the last fully completed cycle. 13,343 candidates qualified for Mains 2026 (UPSC press note).

new.aliases: SSC CGL; CGLE; Combined Graduate Level; SSC graduate level exam
new.eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university (some posts need commerce/maths/statistics background). Age limits vary by post: 18-27, 18-30, 20-30 or 18-32 years on 1 August of the exam year; relaxations for SC/ST, OBC, PwBD, ex-servicemen and others.
new.application_fee: Rs. 100/- (no fee for women, SC/ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen)
new.paper_pattern: Tier-I: 100 objective questions, 200 marks, 1 hour (15-minute sectional timer): General Intelligence & Reasoning, General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude, English Comprehension (25 questions / 50 marks each). Questions in English and Hindi except English section.
new.selection_process: Tier-I (computer-based, qualifying) → Tier-II (computer-based; includes computer knowledge test and data entry speed test, qualifying) → Document verification
new.remarks: Recruits for Group B and C posts (Assistant Section Officer, Inspector, Auditor, Tax Assistant and others) in central ministries. Vacancies are tentative and change during the cycle.

vacancies.note: Approx. 12,256 tentative vacancies in the CGL 2026 notice (21 May 2026), all posts together. An aggregator page later reported 10,731, possibly a revised tentative list; not verified on the SSC site.

new.notes: Exam details from the official CGL 2026 notice (applications 21.05.2026-22.06.2026; window later reopened to 25 June per news). Tier-I 2026 was held around Sept-Oct 2026 per aggregators; applicants given for the completed 2025 cycle. new.exam_name: SSC CHSL (Combined Higher Secondary Level Examination)
new.aliases: SSC CHSL; CHSLE; 10+2 level exam; LDC JSA DEO exam
new.test_date: As per notification (2026 Tier-I dates to be notified)
new.eligibility: Class 12 pass from a recognised board (12th Science with Maths needed for DEO posts in some departments); Class 12 appearing candidates can apply if they pass by the closing date. Age 18-27 years on 1 August of the exam year; relaxations for SC/ST, OBC, PwBD, ex-servicemen and others.
new.application_fee: Rs. 100/- (no fee for women, SC/ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen)
new.paper_pattern: Tier-I: 100 objective questions, 200 marks, 60 minutes (15-minute sectional timer): English Language, General Intelligence, Quantitative Aptitude, General Awareness (25 questions / 50 marks each).
new.selection_process: Tier-I (computer-based, qualifying) → Tier-II (objective papers + skill/typing test, qualifying) → Document verification
new.remarks: Recruits Lower Division Clerk/Junior Secretariat Assistant and Data Entry Operator posts in central offices. Vacancies are tentative and change during the cycle.

applicants.note: CHSL 2025 (Tier-I held 12-30 Nov 2025). Careers360 report on the SSC Tier-I result (27 Feb 2026): about 30.69 lakh applied (rounded), 11,07,975 appeared, 39,901 shortlisted for Tier-II. The SSC result notice itself was not opened. CHSL 2025 had about 3,131 vacancies (news).

vacancies.note: Approx. 2,536 tentative vacancies in the CHSL 2026 notice (7 Sep 2026), all posts together. Copy of the SSC notice hosted on an aggregator site (SSC's notice board could not be fetched directly); the text is the official SSC notice.

new.notes: Details from the CHSL 2026 notice (applications 07.09.2026-07.10.2026; Tier-I schedule 'to be notified later'; an aggregator reports Tier-I in December 2026). CHSL 2026 not yet held, so applicants are from the 2025 cycle.

new.exam_name: SSC MTS (Multi-Tasking Staff and Havaldar Examination)
new.aliases: SSC MTS; Multi Tasking Staff; MTS Havaldar; CBIC Havaldar; peon exam
new.eligibility: Class 10 (Matriculation) pass from a recognised board. Age 18-25 years for MTS and 18-27 years for Havaldar and a few MTS posts, on 1 August of the exam year; relaxations for SC/ST, OBC, PwBD, ex-servicemen and others.
new.application_fee: Rs. 100/- (no fee for women, SC/ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen)
new.paper_pattern: One computer-based exam in two sessions on the same day. Session-I (45 min, no negative marking): Numerical & Mathematical Ability 20 Q/60 marks, Reasoning 20 Q/60 marks. Session-II (45 min, -1 per wrong answer): General Awareness 25 Q/75 marks, English 25 Q/75 marks. Available in Hindi, English and 13 regional languages.
new.selection_process: Computer-based exam → PET/PST (Havaldar only) → Document verification
new.remarks: MTS is a Group C non-technical post in central offices; Havaldar posts are in CBIC and CBN. The 2026 notification had not been checked; confirm dates on the SSC site.
new.notes: Details from the MTS & Havaldar 2025 notice (applications 26.06.2025-24.07.2025, CBE 20 Sep-24 Oct 2025). Vacancies left empty: the 2025 notice gives 1,075 Havaldar vacancies but says MTS vacancies were 'being collected'; an aggregator gives 7,948 combined for 2025 without a source. Applicants left empty: an aggregator claim of 36.17 lakh applicants had no stated source or clear cycle, and no official count was found. An aggregator says the 2026 notification was postponed (expected October 2026); not verified. Copy of the SSC notice hosted on an aggregator site (SSC's notice board could not be fetched directly); the text is the official SSC notice.

new.exam_name: SSC GD (Constable General Duty in CAPFs, SSF and Rifleman in Assam Rifles)
new.aliases: SSC GD; GD Constable; CAPF constable; BSF CRPF CISF constable; Assam Rifles rifleman
new.eligibility: Class 10 (Matriculation) pass. Age 18-23 years on 1 January of the exam year; relaxations for SC/ST, OBC, ex-servicemen and others. Vacancies are state/UT-wise, so a domicile/permanent residence certificate of the state is needed. Physical and medical standards apply.
new.application_fee: Rs. 100/- (no fee for women, SC/ST, ex-servicemen)
new.paper_pattern: 80 objective questions, 2 marks each (160 marks), 60 minutes: General Intelligence & Reasoning, General Knowledge & General Awareness, Elementary Mathematics, English/Hindi (20 questions each). Available in Hindi, English and 13 regional languages.
new.selection_process: Computer-based exam → Physical Standard Test & Physical Efficiency Test → Detailed medical exam → Document verification
new.remarks: Recruits constables for BSF, CISF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB, SSF and riflemen for Assam Rifles. Physical tests are qualifying; merit is on the written exam.

applicants.note: GD 2026 (CBT April-May 2026). Careerpower blog says SSC gave this figure in an RTI reply; the same article also prints 48,83,129 in its breakdown. RTI reply itself not seen.

vacancies.note: 25,487 tentative vacancies (23,467 male + 2,020 female) in the GD 2026 notice (1 Dec 2025). Copy of the SSC notice hosted on an aggregator site (SSC's notice board could not be fetched directly); the text is the official SSC notice.

new.notes: Details from the GD 2026 notice (applications 01.12.2025-31.12.2025, CBE tentatively Feb-April 2026; news says it ran 27 April-30 May 2026). The next (2027) notification is expected around December 2026.

new.exam_name: SSC CPO (Sub-Inspector in Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces)
new.aliases: SSC CPO; SI in Delhi Police and CAPF; CAPF SI; Delhi Police SI; CISF SI Fire
new.test_date: As per notification (2026 Paper-I in late November per news)
new.eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university (Bachelor's in Science with Chemistry for SI Fire in CISF). Age 20-25 years on 1 August of the exam year (18-30 for SI Fire); relaxations for SC/ST, OBC, ex-servicemen and others. Male Delhi Police SI candidates need a valid LMV (motorcycle and car) driving licence by the physical test. Physical and medical standards apply.
new.application_fee: Rs. 100/- (no fee for women, SC/ST, ex-servicemen)
new.paper_pattern: Paper-I: 100 objective questions, 100 marks, 1 hour (15-minute sectional timer): General Intelligence & Reasoning, General Knowledge & General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude, English Comprehension (25 each).
new.selection_process: Paper-I (computer-based) → PST/PET (qualifying) → Paper-II (English) → Detailed medical exam → Document verification
new.remarks: Recruits Sub-Inspectors for Delhi Police, CRPF, BSF, ITBP, CISF and SSB. Women can apply for most posts.

vacancies.note: Delhi Police SI 317 (205 male + 112 female) + CAPF SI (GD) 1,320 (1,173 male + 147 female, combined total) + CISF SI (Fire) 234 = 1,871, per the CPO 2026 notice section 2. Corrected in review from 2,018, which counted the 147 women twice.

new.notes: Details from the CPO 2026 notice (applications 10.09.2026-30.09.2026; CBE schedule 'to be notified later'). Applicants left empty: an aggregator gives about 4,22,917 applicants for 2026 with no official source; no official count found for the completed 2025 cycle.

new.exam_name: Delhi Police Constable (Constable Executive Male and Female in Delhi Police Examination)
new.aliases: Delhi Police Constable; SSC Delhi Police; Delhi Police Constable Executive; DP constable
new.eligibility: Class 12 (10+2) pass from a recognised board (some relaxation for sons of Delhi Police personnel and certain categories). Age 18-25 years on 1 July of the exam year; relaxations for SC/ST, OBC and others. Male candidates need a valid LMV (motorcycle or car) driving licence by the physical test. Open to candidates from all states.
new.application_fee: Rs. 100/- (no fee for women, SC/ST, ex-servicemen)
new.paper_pattern: 100 objective questions, 100 marks, 90 minutes: General Knowledge/Current Affairs 50, Reasoning 25, Numerical Ability 15, Computer Fundamentals (MS Excel, MS Word, internet etc.) 10. English and Hindi only.
new.selection_process: Computer-based exam → Physical Endurance & Measurement Test (qualifying) → Document verification → Medical exam
new.remarks: Conducted by SSC for Delhi Police. Vacancies include separate posts for women and ex-servicemen.

applicants.note: Delhi Police Constable 2025 (CBT Dec 2025-Jan 2026). Adda247 reports 27,25,888 applicants and says it comes from SSC; the SSC document was not seen.

vacancies.note: 7,565 tentative vacancies (Male 4,408 + ex-servicemen 285 + ex-servicemen commando 376; Female 2,496) in the 2025 notice (22 Sep 2025). An aggregator page gives 7,201 (possibly revised); not verified. Copy of the SSC notice hosted on an aggregator site (SSC's notice board could not be fetched directly); the text is the official SSC notice.

new.notes: Details from the 2025 notice (applications 22.09.2025-21.10.2025, later extended to 31.10.2025 per aggregator; CBE Dec 2025-Jan 2026). No 2026 notification found.

new.exam_name: RRB NTPC UG (Non-Technical Popular Categories - Undergraduate Level)
new.aliases: RRB NTPC Undergraduate; RRB NTPC 12th level; Railway NTPC UG; RRB NTPC Under Graduate; NTPC 10+2 level
new.test_date: As per notification (1st stage CBT has been held the following year)
new.eligibility: Class 12 (10+2) or equivalent with at least 50% aggregate marks; the 50% condition does not apply to SC/ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen and candidates with qualifications higher than Class 12. Age 18-30 years (as on 1 January 2027 for CEN 07/2026). Age relaxation exists for SC/ST, OBC (NCL), ex-servicemen and other categories. Candidates awaiting results cannot apply.
new.application_fee: Rs. 500/- (Rs. 400/- refunded on appearing in 1st stage CBT); Rs. 250/- for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, women, transgender, minorities and EBC (fully refunded, less bank charges, on appearing in 1st stage CBT)
new.paper_pattern: 1st stage CBT: 100 objective questions of 1 mark each in 90 minutes - General Awareness 40, Mathematics 30, General Intelligence and Reasoning 30 (section split is indicative). 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer. 2nd stage CBT: 120 questions in 90 minutes (General Awareness 50, Mathematics 35, Reasoning 35).
new.selection_process: 1st stage CBT → 2nd stage CBT → Document verification & medical examination
new.remarks: Posts: Commercial cum Ticket Clerk, Accounts Clerk cum Typist, Junior Clerk cum Typist and Trains Clerk (Pay Level 2-3). From CEN 07/2026 the typing skill test is dropped; typing proficiency is assessed after joining. Apply to only one RRB.

applicants.note: CEN 06/2024 (3,445 vacancies), 1st stage CBT held 7 Aug-9 Sep 2025. PIB release of 4 Feb 2026 (Lok Sabha reply) lists 63,27,473 'candidates' for this CBT. This closely matches the 63,26,818 applications reported by Adda247 from official data, so it is treated as candidates registered/scheduled, not confirmed attendance. 2nd stage CBT: 51,978 candidates (same release).

vacancies.note: CEN 07/2026 (applications 15 Oct-13 Nov 2026): Commercial cum Ticket Clerk 700, Accounts Clerk cum Typist 200, Junior Clerk cum Typist 600, Trains Clerk 188. new.notes: Vacancies are from the latest notice, CEN 07/2026 (exam not yet held as of Nov 2026). Applicants are from the last cycle whose 1st stage CBT is complete with figures published, CEN 06/2024. The intermediate cycle CEN 07/2025 (3,058 vacancies per PIB release of 12 Jun 2026) had CBT-1 in May-Jun 2026 'due for 25 lakh candidates' (PIB); no exact count found. new.exam_name: RRB NTPC Graduate (Non-Technical Popular Categories - Graduate Level)
new.aliases: RRB NTPC Graduate Level; RRB NTPC PG; Railway NTPC Graduate; RRB NTPC Goods Train Manager
new.test_date: As per notification (1st stage CBT has been held the following year)
new.eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university or equivalent. Age 18-33 years (as on 1 January 2027 for CEN 06/2026). Age relaxation exists for SC/ST, OBC (NCL), ex-servicemen and other categories. Candidates awaiting final results cannot apply.
new.application_fee: Rs. 500/- (Rs. 400/- refunded on appearing in 1st stage CBT); Rs. 250/- for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, women, transgender, minorities and EBC (fully refunded, less bank charges, on appearing in 1st stage CBT)
new.paper_pattern: 1st stage CBT: 100 objective questions of 1 mark each in 90 minutes - General Awareness 40, Mathematics 30, General Intelligence and Reasoning 30 (section split is indicative). 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer. 2nd stage CBT: 120 questions in 90 minutes (General Awareness 50, Mathematics 35, Reasoning 35).
new.selection_process: 1st stage CBT → 2nd stage CBT → Document verification & medical examination
new.remarks: Posts in CEN 06/2026: Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor, Goods Train Manager, Junior Accounts Assistant cum Typist, Senior Clerk cum Typist (Pay Level 5-6). Station Master is not in CEN 06/2026 and the typing test was dropped; posts change every notification, so check the CEN.

applicants.note: CEN 05/2024 (8,113 vacancies), 1st stage CBT held 5-24 Jun 2025 (dates per PIB release of 12 Jun 2026). PIB release of 4 Feb 2026 (Lok Sabha reply) lists 58,41,774 'candidates' for this CBT; this closely matches 58,40,861 applications reported by Adda247 from official data, so it is treated as candidates registered/scheduled, not confirmed attendance. 2nd stage CBT: 1,21,931 candidates.

new.notes: Vacancies from the latest notice CEN 06/2026 (exam not yet held). Applicants from CEN 05/2024, the last cycle with an official CBT-1 candidate count. For the intermediate cycle CEN 06/2025 (5,810 vacancies per PIB 12 Jun 2026; CBT-1 16-27 Mar 2026), Adda247 and PW report 25,89,978 tentative applications citing an RRB notice dated 4 Aug 2026; not verified on an official page and not used (the pages also disagree on which RRB had the most applications).

new.exam_name: RRB Group D (Railway Recruitment Board Level 1 Posts)
new.aliases: RRB Group D; Railway Group D; RRB Level 1; RRC Group D; Track Maintainer; Pointsman; Railway Level-1 posts
new.eligibility: Class 10 pass, or ITI, or equivalent, or National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) from NCVT. Age 18-33 years (as on 1 January 2026 for CEN 09/2025). Age relaxation exists for SC/ST, OBC (NCL), PwBD, ex-servicemen and others. Citizens of Nepal and Bhutan and some other categories can also apply as per the CEN.
new.application_fee: Rs. 500/- (Rs. 400/- refunded on appearing in CBT); Rs. 250/- for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, women, transgender, minorities and EBC (fully refunded, less bank charges, on appearing in CBT)
new.paper_pattern: Single CBT: 100 objective questions of 1 mark each in 90 minutes - General Science 25, Mathematics 25, General Intelligence and Reasoning 30, General Awareness and Current Affairs 20 (indicative). 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer. Minimum marks: UR/EWS 40%, OBC/SC/ST 30%.
new.selection_process: CBT → Physical Efficiency Test (PET) → Document verification & medical examination
new.remarks: PET: men lift 35 kg for 100 m in 2 minutes and run 1000 m in 4 min 15 s; women lift 20 kg for 100 m in 2 minutes and run 1000 m in 5 min 40 s. Posts include Track Maintainer, Pointsman and various Assistant posts at Pay Level 1.

vacancies.note: CEN 09/2025 (applications 31 Jan-2 Mar 2026), various Level 1 posts, total of all posts. Read from the updated detailed CEN (testbook.com copy). An earlier copy of the same CEN showed 21,997 and a closing date of 20 Feb 2026, so the CEN was revised. Corrigenda may have changed the count again; not checked. The official RRB/RRC sites blocked automated download.

new.notes: No official applicant count found for any Group D cycle. For CEN 08/2024 (32,438 vacancies; CBT 27 Nov 2025-10 Feb 2026 per PIB), PW reports 'over 1.08 crore candidates' for the Level-1 CBT in an article on RRB recruitment data; the number is rounded and the article does not name an official document, so applicants is left null. Vacancies are from the latest notice, CEN 09/2025; a 2026-27 Level-1 notice was not yet out as of Nov 2026.

new.aliases: RRB ALP; Railway ALP; Assistant Loco Pilot; Railway Loco Pilot recruitment; RRB Loco Pilot
new.eligibility: Class 10 (Matriculation/SSLC) plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT in a listed trade (e.g. Fitter, Electrician, Mechanic Diesel, Turner, Machinist), or Class 10 plus Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in those trades, or Class 10 plus a 3-year diploma (or degree) in Mechanical/Electrical/Electronics/Automobile Engineering. Class 10 alone is not enough. Age 18-30 years (as on 1 July 2026 for CEN 01/2026); relaxations exist for SC/ST, OBC (NCL), ex-servicemen and others. Medical standard A-1 (strict eyesight); not suitable for PwBD.
new.application_fee: Rs. 500/- (Rs. 400/- refunded on appearing in CBT-1); Rs. 250/- for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, women, transgender, minorities and EBC (fully refunded, less bank charges, on appearing in CBT-1)
new.paper_pattern: CBT-1 (screening only): 75 objective questions of 1 mark in 60 minutes on Mathematics, Mental Ability and General Science (Class 10 level); 1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer. CBT-2: Part A 100 questions in 90 minutes, Part B (trade, qualifying 35%) 75 questions in 60 minutes.
new.selection_process: CBT-1 (screening) → CBT-2 (Part A + trade Part B) → Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) → Document verification & medical examination
new.remarks: Final merit uses CBT-2 Part A and CBAT scores 50:50; CBAT has no negative marking and each test battery must be cleared. Candidates must pass a strict A-1 medical (vision) standard.

applicants.note: CEN 01/2024 (18,799 vacancies), the latest fully completed ALP cycle (17,193 empanelled per PIB 12 Jun 2026). PIB release of 4 Feb 2026 lists 18,40,347 'candidates' for the 1st stage CBT; treated as candidates registered/scheduled, not confirmed attendance. CBT-2: 2,66,363; CBAT: 1,32,044 (same release).

vacancies.note: CEN 01/2026: 11,127 vacancies in the detailed CEN of 14 May 2026, raised to 14,627 by Amendment/Corrigendum No. 1 dated 10 Nov 2026 (read from an adda247.com copy of the official corrigendum, file named as RRB Chennai). Total of all RRBs.

new.notes: Stage is After Class 10 because the base requirement is Class 10, but ITI/apprenticeship/diploma in a listed trade is also required. Vacancies from the latest notice CEN 01/2026 (CBT-1 reported by Adda247 as held 3-5 Nov 2026; not verified officially). Applicants from CEN 01/2024. The intermediate cycle CEN 01/2025 had 10,970 vacancies per PIB 12 Jun 2026 (PW lists 9,970 at notification); its CBT-1 count was not found.

new.aliases: IBPS PO; IBPS PO/MT; CRP PO/MT; IBPS Probationary Officer; Bank PO; IBPS Management Trainee
new.test_date: Prelims in August; Mains in October
new.marking: 1/4 of the question's marks deducted per wrong answer; no penalty for unanswered questions
new.eligibility: A degree (graduation) in any discipline from a recognised university, with the result declared by the closing date of registration (21.07.2026 in the 2026 cycle). Age 20 to 30 years as on 01.07.2026 (born 02.07.1996 to 01.07.2006); upper age relaxations exist for SC/ST (5 years), OBC-NCL (3 years), PwBD (10 years), ex-servicemen and others.
new.paper_pattern: Online Prelims, 100 questions for 100 marks in 60 minutes, three separately timed sections of 20 minutes each: English Language (30 Q, 30 marks), Quantitative Aptitude (35 Q, 30 marks), Reasoning Ability (35 Q, 40 marks). Candidates must clear the cut-off in each section. Mains has 170 objective questions for 200 marks (Reasoning; General/Economy/Banking/Digital/Financial Awareness; English; Data Analysis & Interpretation) in 160 minutes, plus a 25-mark descriptive paper (essay and comprehension) in 30 minutes.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective, qualifying) → Mains (objective + descriptive) → Personality Test (non-qualifying, compulsory) → Interview (Mains:Interview weightage 80:20) → Provisional allotment to a participating bank
new.remarks: One common exam for PO/MT posts in 11 public sector banks (excluding SBI); vacancies are indicative and are updated by corrigenda during the cycle. Confirm the latest figures on ibps.in.

vacancies.note: CRP PO/MT-XVI (2026 cycle, vacancies of 2027-28): total of participating banks' indicative (tentative) vacancies in updated Annexure I as on 27.08.2026 (corrigendum dated 27.08.2026). Union Bank of India had not reported vacancies (NR). The original notification dated 01.07.2026 listed 6,715 (Indian Bank, UCO Bank and Union Bank NR). The 2025 cycle (CRP PO/MT-XV) notification listed 5,208.

new.notes: All pattern, eligibility, fee and timing details are from the CRP PO/MT-XVI (2026) notification dated 01.07.2026. The 2026 cycle is not complete: Mains results came out on 20.11.2026; personality test and interviews are scheduled for Nov/Dec 2026 and allotment for Jan 2027. The 2025 cycle (XV) is the latest completed one. Applicants left null: IBPS does not publish registered/appeared counts for CRP PO on ibps.in (its Growth page gives only older combined figures as charts), and I found no Ministry of Finance/parliament answer. Aggregator pages claim about 12.35 lakh applied for IBPS PO 2025, but they give no official attribution, so it was not used.

new.aliases: IBPS Clerk; IBPS CSA; CRP CSA; CRP Clerical Cadre; IBPS Customer Service Associate; Bank Clerk
new.test_date: Prelims in October; Mains in December
new.marking: +1/-0.25 in Prelims (1/4 of the question's marks deducted per wrong answer; no penalty for unanswered questions)
new.eligibility: A degree (graduation) in any discipline from a recognised university, held on the day of registration; computer literacy (certificate/diploma/degree in computers or computers studied as a subject in school/college). Must be able to read, write, speak and understand the official local language of the State/UT applied for. Age 20 to 28 years as on 01.08.2026 (born 02.08.1998 to 01.08.2006); upper age relaxations exist for SC/ST, OBC-NCL, PwBD, ex-servicemen and others.
new.paper_pattern: Online Prelims, 100 questions for 100 marks in 60 minutes, three separately timed sections of 20 minutes each: English Language (30 Q, 30 marks), Numerical Ability (35 Q, 35 marks), Reasoning Ability (35 Q, 35 marks). Candidates must clear the cut-off in each section. Mains has 160 questions for 200 marks in 125 minutes (General/Financial Awareness, General English, Reasoning Ability, Quantitative Aptitude). Tests other than English are offered in Hindi and the regional language of many States.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective, qualifying) → Mains (objective; final merit on Mains marks only) → Local Language Proficiency Test (qualifying) → Provisional allotment to a participating bank
new.remarks: Candidates apply for vacancies in one State/UT and must know its local language; there is no interview. Vacancies are indicative and are revised during the cycle, so check ibps.in.

vacancies.note: CRP CSA-XVI (2026 cycle, vacancies of 2027-28): sum of the 37 State/UT totals in the updated Annexure I as on 29.09.2026 (corrigendum dated 29.09.2026). These are the participating banks' indicative (tentative) vacancies; Union Bank of India had not reported (NR). The notification dated 01.08.2026 listed 11,403.
